title: Invariant Property Observation for Permutation Swaps
approach_explanation:
The problem permits swapping $a_i$ and $a_{i+1}$ if $a_{i-1} < a_i$ and $a_i > a_{i+1}$. Notice that the operation can only be applied at indices $2  iguplus n-1$ (1-indexed). This implies that the very first element $a_1$ and the very last element $a_n$ can never be directly involved as the moving element of the swap because $i$ cannot be $1$ or $n$. Specifically, the first element $a_1$ can never move to the right because no index allows a swap where the first element is the middle element. Therefore, if $a_1 
eq 1$, $1$ can never be moved to its correct position at the front of the permutation, making it impossible to sort. Conversely, if $a_1 = 1$, we can always bubble elements to their correct sorted positions using bubble sort-like logic with the available operation.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$ and loops through each test case.
Reads the size $n$ of the permutation and the $n$ elements into a vector.
Checks if the first element of the array is $1$. If numbers[0] != 1, outputs 'NO', otherwise outputs 'YES'.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each test case, we read $n$ elements in a single pass of length $n$. Across $t$ test cases, the total time complexity is $O(\sum n)$, which is at most $5000 \times 10 = 50,000$ operations, well within the 1-second time limit.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: A vector of size $n$ is allocated for each test case to store the permutation. Since $n \le 10$, this uses negligible memory.

strengths: Extremely concise and hits the core mathematical invariant of the problem immediately.
best_practices_feedback: Use '\n' instead of 'endl' for faster I/O in competitive programming.
Include 'ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(NULL);' for optimal competitive performance.

optimization_and_alternatives.approach_name: Direct Input Check without Vector Storage
optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Instead of storing the entire permutation in a vector, we can read the first element and consume the rest of the inputs on the fly, reducing auxiliary space complexity to $O(1)$.
